answer.summary: Rollout analysis run ar-efc877ae returned verdict degradation while phase is Progressing. Ingress 5xx ratio jumped from about 0.2% to 6-7% starting 12 minutes ago, immediately after revision 203 was deployed 11 minutes ago. Request rate, p99 latency, CPU and PostgreSQL query latency are all flat, so this is not a capacity or database problem. The self-reported app 5xx metric staying low is only supporting evidence and does not change the verdict. Proposing abort and rollback of the canary with reason canary_degradation.

Kafka consumer lag for pricing-svc grew continuously from about 200 to over 130000 messages across the 30-minute window and is still rising in the last 5 minutes, so this is not a transient spike. CPU utilization climbed in parallel to 0.94, indicating the consumers are saturated and cannot keep up with the incoming event rate. Replicas (3) are below the maximum (6), so scaling out adds consumer capacity to drain the backlog. No active rollout and the last deploy was about 60 hours ago, so this is not release-related.

The last 5 values show request rate ~104 rps, CPU ~0.49 and p99 ~147 ms, matching the starting level. No active rollout and the last deploy was ~55 hours ago, so this is not release-related. The spike has passed and the autoscaler (3 replicas, max 6) absorbed it; no scaling or restart action is warranted.

External ingress 5xx ratio jumped from about 0.002 to about 0.044 and stays elevated in the last 5 minutes; the analysis metric shows canary 0.0744 vs baseline 0.0025, Holm significant. Self-reported app 5xx, p99 latency, CPU and PostgreSQL p95 are flat, so the regression is specific to the new revision, not capacity or the database. Propose aborting the canary and rolling back to stable revision 298 with reason canary_degradation.
